title: Book Review: The Happiness Industry: How the Government and Big Business Sold Us Well-Being
subtitle: Book Review
author: By William Davies
overallInstruction: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27–40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.
overallInstructionZh: 你应该用大约20分钟完成第27—40题；这些题目以以下阅读文章3为依据。

footnote.text: * ‘behaviourism’: a branch of psychology which is concerned with observable behaviour
footnote.translationZh: * behaviourism（行为主义）：心理学的一个分支，研究可观察到的行为。
footnote.note: This explanatory fragment is not counted as a body sentence.

sentences: ‘Happiness is the ultimate goal because it is self-evidently good.
If we are asked why happiness matters we can give no further external reason.
It just obviously does matter.’
This pronouncement by Richard Layard, an economist and advocate of ‘positive psychology’, summarises the beliefs of many people today.
For Layard and others like him, it is obvious that the purpose of government is to promote a state of collective well-being.

The only question is how to achieve it, and here positive psychology – a supposed science that not only identifies what makes people happy but also allows their happiness to be measured – can show the way.
Equipped with this science, they say, governments can secure happiness in society in a way they never could in the past.
It is an astonishingly crude and simple-minded way of thinking, and for that very reason increasingly popular.

Those who think in this way are oblivious to the vast philosophical literature in which the meaning and value of happiness have been explored and questioned, and write as if nothing of any importance had been thought on the subject until it came to their attention.
It was the philosopher Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832) who was more than anyone else responsible for the development of this way of thinking.
For Bentham it was obvious that the human good consists of pleasure and the absence of pain.

The Greek philosopher Aristotle may have identified happiness with self-realisation in the 4th century BC, and thinkers throughout the ages may have struggled to reconcile the pursuit of happiness with other human values, but for Bentham all this was mere metaphysics or fiction.

Without knowing anything much of him or the school of moral theory he established – since they are by education and intellectual conviction illiterate in the history of ideas – our advocates of positive psychology follow in his tracks in rejecting as outmoded and irrelevant pretty much the entirety of ethical reflection on human happiness to date.
But as William Davies notes in his recent book The Happiness Industry, the view that happiness is the only self-evident good is actually a way of limiting moral inquiry.
One of the virtues of this rich, lucid and arresting book is that it places the current cult of happiness in a well-defined historical framework.
Rightly, Davies begins his story with Bentham, noting that he was far more than a philosopher.
Davies writes, ‘Bentham’s activities were those which we might now associate with a public sector management consultant’.

In the 1790s, he wrote to the Home Office suggesting that the departments of government be linked together through a set of ‘conversation tubes’, and to the Bank of England with a design for a printing device that could produce unforgeable banknotes.
He drew up plans for a ‘frigidarium’ to keep provisions such as meat, fish, fruit and vegetables fresh.
His celebrated design for a prison to be known as a ‘Panopticon’, in which prisoners would be kept in solitary confinement while being visible at all times to the guards, was very nearly adopted.
(Surprisingly, Davies does not discuss the fact that Bentham meant his Panopticon not just as a model prison but also as an instrument of control that could be applied to schools and factories.)
Bentham was also a pioneer of the ‘science of happiness’.
If happiness is to be regarded as a science, it has to be measured, and Bentham suggested two ways in which this might be done.
Viewing happiness as a complex of pleasurable sensations, he suggested that it might be quantified by measuring the human pulse rate.
Alternatively, money could be used as the standard for quantification: if two different goods have the same price, it can be claimed that they produce the same quantity of pleasure in the consumer.
Bentham was more attracted by the latter measure.

By associating money so closely to inner experience, Davies writes, Bentham ‘set the stage for the entangling of psychological research and capitalism that would shape the business practices of the twentieth century’.
The Happiness Industry describes how the project of a science of happiness has become integral to capitalism.
We learn much that is interesting about how economic problems are being redefined and treated as psychological maladies.
In addition, Davies shows how the belief that inner states of pleasure and displeasure can be objectively measured has informed management studies and advertising.
The tendency of thinkers such as J B Watson, the founder of behaviourism*, was that human beings could be shaped, or manipulated, by policymakers and managers.
Watson had no factual basis for his view of human action.
When he became president of the American Psychological Association in 1915, he ‘had never even studied a single human being’: his research had been confined to experiments on white rats.

Yet Watson’s reductive model is now widely applied, with ‘behaviour change’ becoming the goal of governments: in Britain, a ‘Behaviour Insights Team’ has been established by the government to study how people can be encouraged, at minimum cost to the public purse, to live in what are considered to be socially desirable ways.
Modern industrial societies appear to need the possibility of ever-increasing happiness to motivate them in their labours.
But whatever its intellectual pedigree, the idea that governments should be responsible for promoting happiness is always a threat to human freedom.

questionSections.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 27–29 on your answer sheet.
questionSections.instructionZh: 选择正确字母A、B、C或D，并把正确字母写在答题纸第27—29格。

questionSections.instruction: Complete the summary using the list of words A–G below. Write the correct letter, A–G, in boxes 30–34 on your answer sheet.
questionSections.instructionZh: 用下方A—G词表完成摘要，并把正确字母写在答题纸第30—34格。
questionSections.summary: Jeremy Bentham was active in other areas besides philosophy. In the 1790s he suggested a type of technology to improve 30 __________ for different Government departments. He developed a new way of printing banknotes to increase 31 __________ and also designed a method for the 32 __________ of food. He also drew up plans for a prison which allowed the 33 __________ of prisoners at all times, and believed the same design could be used for other institutions as well. When researching happiness, he investigated possibilities for its 34 __________, and suggested some methods of doing this.
questionSections.summaryZh: 杰里米·边沁除哲学外还活跃于其他领域。18世纪90年代，他提出一种技术，用于改善不同政府部门之间的30__________。他开发了新的纸币印刷方式以提高31__________，还设计了食物32__________的方法。他也规划了一座可随时33__________囚犯的监狱，并认为同一设计还能用于其他机构。研究幸福时，他探讨了对幸福进行34__________的可能性，并提出若干方法。

questionSections.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3? In boxes 35–40 on your answer sheet, write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer; NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer; NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
questionSections.instructionZh: 下列陈述是否与作者观点一致？一致写YES；相矛盾写NO；无法判断作者观点写NOT GIVEN。

labels.label: NOT GIVEN
labels.translationZh: 无法从文中判断作者观点

questions.prompt: What is the reviewer’s attitude to advocates of positive psychology?
questions.translationZh: 评论者对积极心理学倡导者持什么态度？

options.label: A
options.text: They are wrong to reject the ideas of Bentham.
options.translationZh: 他们拒绝边沁的思想是错误的。

options.label: B
options.text: They are over-influenced by their study of Bentham’s theories.
options.translationZh: 他们因研究边沁理论而受其过度影响。

options.label: C
options.text: They have a fresh new approach to ideas on human happiness.
options.translationZh: 他们以全新方式看待人类幸福。

options.label: D
options.text: They are ignorant about the ideas they should be considering.
options.translationZh: 他们不了解本应纳入考虑的思想。

questions.evidence: our advocates of positive psychology ... are ... illiterate in the history of ideas
questions.reasoning: illiterate in the history of ideas直接对应ignorant about the ideas。
questions.distractors: A错误：作者不是批评他们拒绝边沁，而是说他们不自知地追随边沁；B错误：他们对边沁所知甚少，并非受深入研究过度影响；C错误：作者说他们忽视思想史，并非赞扬其新颖；D正确：illiterate in the history of ideas 对应 ignorant about the ideas。

questions.prompt: The reviewer refers to the Greek philosopher Aristotle in order to suggest that happiness
questions.translationZh: 评论者提到希腊哲学家亚里士多德，是为了说明幸福……

options.label: A
options.text: may not be just pleasure and the absence of pain.
options.translationZh: 可能不只是快乐和没有痛苦。

options.label: B
options.text: should not be the main goal of humans.
options.translationZh: 不应成为人类的主要目标。

options.label: C
options.text: is not something that should be fought for.

options.label: D
options.text: is not just an abstract concept.

questions.evidence: Aristotle may have identified happiness with self-realisation ... but for Bentham all this was mere metaphysics
questions.reasoning: 亚里士多德以自我实现界定幸福，显示幸福不只等于快乐且无痛苦。
questions.distractors: A正确：self-realisation证明幸福不只等于快乐且无痛；B错误：原文没有说幸福不应成为主要目标；C错误：原文没有反对争取幸福；D错误：此处比较幸福定义，而非抽象与具体。

questions.prompt: According to Davies, Bentham’s suggestion for linking the price of goods to happiness was significant because
questions.translationZh: 据戴维斯说，边沁把商品价格与幸福联系起来的建议之所以重要，是因为……

options.label: A
options.text: it was the first successful way of assessing happiness.
options.translationZh: 这是首个成功评估幸福的方法。

options.label: B
options.text: it established a connection between work and psychology.
options.translationZh: 它在商业活动与心理学之间建立了联系。

options.label: C
options.text: it was the first successful example of psychological research.
options.translationZh: 这是心理学研究首次成功的例子。

options.label: D
options.text: it involved consideration of the rights of consumers.
options.translationZh: 它涉及对消费者权利的考虑。

questions.evidence: set the stage for the entangling of psychological research and capitalism that would shape the business practices
questions.reasoning: psychological research与capitalism/business practices的联系对应B。
questions.distractors: A错误：原文未称这是首个成功评估方法；B正确：对应心理研究与资本主义商业实践的联结；C错误：原文未称其为首个成功心理研究；D错误：全文没有讨论消费者权利。

questions.prompt: technology to improve __________ for different Government departments
questions.translationZh: 改善不同政府部门之间的__________的技术
questions.evidence: departments of government be linked together through a set of ‘conversation tubes’
questions.distractors: A measurement属于幸福量化；B security属于纸币防伪；C implementation无原文对应；D profits无原文对应；E observation属于监狱监视；F communication正确；G preservation属于食物保鲜。

questions.prompt: a new way of printing banknotes to increase __________
questions.translationZh: 新的纸币印刷方式，以提高__________
questions.evidence: a printing device that could produce unforgeable banknotes
questions.distractors: A measurement不等于防伪；B security正确；C implementation未提；D profits未提；E observation对应监狱监视；F communication对应部门联络；G preservation对应食物保鲜。

questions.prompt: a method for the __________ of food
questions.distractors: A measurement对应幸福量化；B security对应纸币防伪；C implementation未提；D profits未提；E observation对应监狱监视；F communication对应部门联络；G preservation正确，对应keep ... fresh。

questions.prompt: a prison which allowed the __________ of prisoners at all times
questions.translationZh: 一座允许随时__________囚犯的监狱
questions.evidence: prisoners would be ... visible at all times to the guards
questions.distractors: A measurement对应幸福量化；B security不是该监狱设计在此强调的功能；C implementation未提；D profits未提；E observation正确；F communication对应部门联络；G preservation对应食物保鲜。

questions.evidence: If happiness is to be regarded as a science, it has to be measured
questions.distractors: A measurement正确；B security是纸币防伪；C implementation未提；D profits不是文中的价格衡量；E observation是监狱监视；F communication是部门联络；G preservation是食物保鲜。

questions.prompt: One strength of The Happiness Industry is its discussion of the relationship between psychology and economics.
questions.translationZh: 《幸福产业》的一个优点是讨论了心理学与经济学之间的关系。
questions.evidence: One of the virtues ...; ... entangling of psychological research and capitalism; ... economic problems ... psychological maladies
questions.reasoning: 作者称书有virtues，并肯定其揭示心理研究与资本主义/经济问题的关系。
questions.distractors: NO与称赞相反；NOT GIVEN不成立，因为关系被明确讨论。

questions.prompt: It is more difficult to measure some emotions than others.
questions.translationZh: 有些情绪比另一些更难测量。
questions.evidence: Viewing happiness as a complex of pleasurable sensations, he suggested that it might be quantified by measuring the human pulse rate. / In addition, Davies shows how the belief that inner states of pleasure and displeasure can be objectively measured has informed management studies and advertising.
questions.reasoning: 两处只讨论幸福或愉悦/不悦可被测量，没有比较some emotions与others的测量难度。
questions.distractors: YES不成立：可测量性不能推出不同情绪难度有别；NO不成立：原文也没有说所有情绪同样容易；NOT GIVEN正确：缺少比较维度。

questions.prompt: Watson’s ideas on behaviourism were supported by research on humans he carried out before 1915.
questions.translationZh: 沃森关于行为主义的观点得到了他在1915年前开展的人体研究的支持。
questions.evidence: he ‘had never even studied a single human being’: his research had been confined to experiments on white rats
questions.reasoning: 题干称有人体研究；原文明确从未研究人，只研究白鼠。
questions.distractors: YES与原文相反；NOT GIVEN不成立，因为研究对象明确。

questions.prompt: Watson’s ideas have been most influential on governments outside America.
questions.translationZh: 沃森的思想对美国以外的政府影响最大。
questions.evidence: Yet Watson’s reductive model is now widely applied, with ‘behaviour change’ becoming the goal of governments: in Britain, a ‘Behaviour Insights Team’ has been established by the government to study how people can be encouraged, at minimum cost to the public purse, to live in what are considered to be socially desirable ways.
questions.reasoning: 原文只举英国实例，没有比较美国内外的影响程度，更没有most influential最高级依据。
questions.distractors: YES不成立：英国例子不能推出美国以外影响最大；NO不成立：原文也未说美国影响更大；NOT GIVEN正确：缺少地域与程度比较。

questions.prompt: The need for happiness is linked to industrialisation.
questions.translationZh: 对幸福的需要与工业化有关。
questions.evidence: Modern industrial societies appear to need the possibility of ever-increasing happiness to motivate them in their labours.
questions.reasoning: industrial societies与need ... happiness直接建立联系。
questions.distractors: NO与原句相反；NOT GIVEN不成立，因为联系明确。

questions.prompt: A main aim of government should be to increase the happiness of the population.
questions.translationZh: 政府的一项主要目标应是提高民众幸福。
questions.evidence: the idea that governments should be responsible for promoting happiness is always a threat to human freedom
questions.reasoning: 作者认为政府负责促进幸福会威胁自由，与题干应当如此相反。
questions.distractors: YES混淆Layard的主张与评论者立场；NOT GIVEN不成立，因为末句明确表态。
